s1.syndrome_frame: Acute to subacute neurological deterioration with fever and focal neurological deficits
salient_findings: Altered mental status
Left upper- and lower-limb weakness
Hypodense area in the right basal ganglia with mass effect on head CT
T2/FLAIR hyperintensity in the right basal ganglia and internal capsule on brain MRI
Pleocytosis and elevated protein in cerebrospinal fluid
Progression of neurological deficits and imaging findings despite empirical antibiotic treatment
key_facts: 19-year-old man with hepatitis C and intravenous heroin use
Transferred for evaluation of altered mental status
Minimally responsive and febrile on arrival
Glasgow Coma Scale 10
Required intubation for airway protection
Left upper- and lower-limb weakness (strength 2/5 and 3/5)
No meningeal signs
Vital signs were stable
Leukocytosis (white blood cell count rising from 10.0 to 14.6 × 10^3/µL)
Urine toxicology positive for benzodiazepines and opiates
Noncontrast head CT showed hypodense area in the right basal ganglia with mass effect
Brain MRI showed T2/FLAIR hyperintensity in the right basal ganglia and internal capsule
Lumbar puncture yielded cerebrospinal fluid with 538 WBCs/mm³ and protein 81 mg/dL
Empirical IV ceftriaxone, vancomycin, and acyclovir were begun
Leukocytosis improved but fever persisted
Repeat lumbar puncture showed increased opening pressure and pleocytosis
Repeat MRI demonstrated progression with new involvement of the left basal ganglia
